Description: We are seeking an experienced data engineer to develop an existing collection of podcast, media and related directory data into a reliable, useful and maintainable commercial database. Our first use case is podcast guest and expert outreach research: helping users identify relevant programmes, understand their topics and guest patterns, assess information freshness, and find supported professional contact or booking routes. CURRENT POSITION Our saved inventory contains approximately 6.58 million source rows across 24 inputs, including around 1.87 million podcast listing IDs. Sources overlap and contain different record types; these figures are not counts of unique people or fully verified podcasts. Existing assets include Press Hunt and Rephonic exports, consolidated databases, Python scripts, cached episode evidence, quality reports and a basic searchable interface. Validation and enrichment are incomplete. We want you to assess and reuse valuable existing work, simplify inefficient processes, and deliver a sustainable production system. Other directory categories will follow using the same core infrastructure. SCOPE OF WORK 1. Audit and architecture Reconcile the source inventory, assess existing code and data, identify missing source versions and quality gaps, and recommend a practical architecture. Provide an implementation plan with clear costs, milestones, acceptance criteria and a recommendation on which existing components to retain or replace. Flag source licensing and permitted-use questions requiring resolution before commercial release. 2. Consolidation and deduplication Establish a canonical schema and stable identifiers. Resolve overlapping records while distinguishing programmes, episodes, hosts, guests, publishers, organisations and contacts. Preserve original sources, historical values, source mappings, exclusions and suppression records. Keep uncertain matches separate and make changes reversible. 3. Validation Check identities, programme attribution, websites, RSS feeds, URLs, publication dates, activity, language, geography and professional contact routes where supported. Clearly distinguish verified, historical, missing, conflicting and unverifiable information. Technical email validation, current affiliation, booking relevance, deliverability and permission to contact must remain separate states. Do not invent missing information. Maintain an exception queue so isolated record problems do not stop unrelated processing. 4. Useful and distinctive enrichment Add supported information such as recent topics, attributable host and guest credits, interview formats, publishing cadence, episode duration, relevant episode examples, guest-submission instructions and source dates. Evaluate additional commercially useful fields, such as recurring guest profiles, topic changes, repeat-guest frequency and evidence-supported pitch suggestions. Recommend which enrichment fields provide sufficient usefulness, coverage and differentiation to justify their processing and maintenance costs. Separate verified facts, calculated measures, estimates and editorial or AI suggestions. Do not assume that a field is unique without checking competing offerings. 5. Accessible database Provide a working searchable database with useful filters, programme profiles, supporting evidence, freshness labels and CSV exports. Provide documented structured data access for future integrations. Use client-owned storage, repositories and service accounts. Include appropriate access controls for restricted contact fields. A public subscription platform, billing system and campaign sending are outside the initial scope. 6. Ongoing refresh, maintenance and expansion Implement scheduled updates, change detection and incremental processing so unchanged data is not repeatedly reprocessed. Prioritise refresh according to publication activity, field volatility, usage and business value. Handle rate limits, retries, source changes, broken feeds, redirects, rebrands and duplicates. Provide monitoring, alerts, backups, a tested restore procedure and clear maintenance instructions. Implement an approved process for discovering, assessing and adding new programmes and sources without introducing duplicates. 7. Cost control Minimise unnecessary scraping, model calls and manual review. Prefer structured sources, RSS, APIs and deterministic processing where appropriate. Scrapfly and Bright Data may be available. Assess whether they are needed, verify integration before relying on them, and recommend alternatives where justified. Itemise engineering labour, routine human review, hosting, storage, verification, scraping, AI usage and ongoing support costs. Provide spending limits, bounded retries and transparent usage reporting. No unapproved purchases, large paid runs or dependence on personal vendor accounts. DELIVERY APPROACH Begin with a paid, bounded discovery milestone. Follow this with a proposed representative 1,000-record pilot, covering different sources and quality conditions rather than only easy records. Include duplicates, ambiguous identities, missing feeds and inactive programmes. The pilot must demonstrate: - Working ingestion, validation and selected enrichment. - Usable search and export. - Independently reviewed quality. - Processing throughput and actual operating costs. - Safe restart after interruption. - Refresh behaviour that avoids unnecessary repeat processing. Production rollout will follow agreed acceptance criteria. Quote baseline processing across the full population separately from richer enrichment of commercially useful segments. QUALITY REQUIREMENTS Every newly populated factual enrichment must be traceable to its source and check date. Unsupported values must remain unknown. Report matching accuracy, field accuracy, coverage, freshness and unresolved cases separately. AI confidence scores alone are not independent verification. Existing failed or unresolved batches must remain excluded until a documented correction and release process succeeds. Sending outreach is outside this engagement. DELIVERABLES The database, source code, schema and data dictionary, source mappings, automated jobs, searchable interface, quality reports, cost reporting, migration and rollback procedures, maintenance schedule, backup/restore instructions and operational handover. Client-specific deliverables must remain maintainable by another engineer using client-owned accounts. Disclose third-party components and licence obligations. APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS Provide two comparable projects, your personal contribution, dataset sizes, quality measures and ongoing costs. Include your proposed approach, assumptions, delivery schedule and separate discovery, pilot, production and maintenance quotations. Identify who will perform the technical work and disclose proposed subcontracting. Any substantial trial implementation will be paid. We are seeking a long-term technical partner, beginning with one bounded milestone and measurable delivery.
